title: Flaky unit test: unhandled rejection 'Folder is outside the allowed photo locations' during folder.spec.ts
description: Main CI run 38934298706 (commit 68495d2) failed in the quality job: Vitest 'caught 1 unhandled error during the test run', Error: Folder is outside the allowed photo locations (HUB_PHOTO_ROOTS), 'originated in src/lib/server/photo-source/folder.spec.ts'. The previous main run (45b95b1) passed, so it's intermittent: some promise (fire-and-forget scan/prerender, or the backupIdle/prerenderIdle tracking that #86 added in src/lib/server/backup.ts, photo-source/prerender.ts and shutdown.ts) rejects with nobody awaiting it, and its timing decides whether Vitest sees it inside the run. Find the unawaited promise, handle or await it correctly in the app (a fire-and-forget rejection in production is also an unhandled rejection that can crash Node), make the test deterministic, and prove it with many repeated runs (vitest --repeat or a loop of 30 runs of the photo-source and backup specs).

title: Photo library settings: stale refreshes overwrite newer state (flaky photo-library e2e)

Discard stale refreshes with a generation counter; e2e must wait for the scan to finish (not match 'scanned' already on screen).

title: interaction-perf gates flake on CI (nav input delay 111.5 ms, approve handlers 110.5 ms)
description: tests/e2e/interaction-perf.e2e.ts (from #83; nav check changed in #87, cold tap tightened in #89) flakes on CI: PR #88 failed twice on unrelated CSS-only changes, first 'nav: input delay' 111.5 ms vs 100, then 'approve: handlers' 110.5 ms vs 100 (portrait). In #83's own CI, approve handlers were 47-53 ms, so CI variance is large: two Playwright projects run in parallel on a small runner at 4x CPU throttle, alongside the rest of the suite. Fix the gate so it is stable on CI while still catching real regressions: (1) gather the [perf ...] log lines from every recent CI e2e run (gh run list --workflow CI, gh run view --log, grep '[perf') to get real CI distributions per measure; (2) reduce measurement noise: tap only on an idle page (network idle, fonts, animations done, a couple of requestIdleCallback turns), and keep perf measurements from competing with each other (e.g. split measures across the two projects instead of running every perf test in both, the way portrait-layout split viewports; check the CI runner core count); (3) pick budgets with clear headroom against the CI max (ADR 0002's 100 ms INP target can stay as the gate only if CI data supports it; otherwise document the CI-calibrated budget and keep 100 as the local/target figure in a comment). No skips; don't drop measures without explanation.

title: Server ignores SIGTERM: docker stop waits 10s then SIGKILLs mid-write
description: Found while cleaning up orphaned e2e servers: 266 'node build' processes (reparented to PID 1, no listening socket) all ignored SIGTERM and needed SIGKILL. In production, docker stop / compose restart / a deploy sends SIGTERM (compose uses init: true, so tini forwards it); if the app ignores it, Docker waits 10s and then SIGKILLs it, possibly mid-write with SQLite open. Find what keeps the process alive or swallows SIGTERM (a custom process.on('SIGTERM') handler, open SSE connections, backup/scan timers, the photo prerender queue, an unclosed better-sqlite3 handle). Make shutdown graceful: stop accepting, end SSE streams, clear timers, close the DB, and exit within ~2s. Add a test that spawns the built server, sends SIGTERM with an SSE client connected, and asserts exit within 3s with code 0. This also explains the orphaned e2e servers piling up locally.

title: Cold first 'I did it!' tap costs 80-270 ms of handler time at 4x CPU (over 100 ms INP budget)
description: Found by tests/e2e/interaction-perf.e2e.ts (hub-ugl.4.5). At 4x CPU throttle the FIRST tap on a freshly loaded kid chores page spends ~77-270 ms (typically 95-185) in the click event's processing (Event Timing processingEnd-processingStart); the second tap spends ~10-18 ms. Only 'celebrate' User Timing scripting is ~2-10 ms, so the rest is cold-path cost (first-time layout/style, lazy init, JIT) in the Svelte flush or elsewhere in the click task. Two long tasks follow the tap (~100 + ~70 ms). Needs profiling (CDP Profiler/Tracing) and a fix (pre-warm during idle, e.g. force layout/render a pending slot, avoid first-use work in the tap). Then tighten checkTap('I did it (cold)') budgetMs to 100 in interaction-perf.e2e.ts.

There is plenty of width for both on one row (clock is about 600px, controls about 1300px, header about 2100px), so roughly 110px of vertical space is lost on every wall screen. Find what forces the wrap (likely a flex-basis or width on the clock link or column) and keep one row in landscape while portrait still wraps cleanly. title: Add project README

title: photo-library e2e: new folder card can take >5s to appear in CI
description: After #60 fixed the refresh race, #65's first CI run still failed photo-library.e2e.ts waiting 5s for the new folder card (rerun passed; not reproducible locally in 5 runs). POST /api/photo-sources scans and pre-renders synchronously before responding, so under CI load with both viewport projects adding folders the response can exceed the default expect timeout. Options: respond after scan but pre-render in the background, or show the card immediately with a scanning state. Don't just raise the timeout without understanding the cost.
close_reason: Merged in #73 (POST was already fast; card now renders from the POST response)

title: Sound settings UI: mute + quiet hours

title: Phone layout polish (approvals + shell at 390px)

title: Primary nav gives no instant feedback: active tab updates only after route load (3-4 frames, ~90-160 ms at 4x)
description: Found by tests/e2e/interaction-perf.e2e.ts (hub-ugl.4.5). Tapping a nav link, aria-current moves only after SvelteKit finishes the navigation, 3-4 rAF frames (86-160 ms after pointerdown at 4x CPU). ADR 0002 wants the first visual response in the tapped frame or the next. Add an optimistic pending/active state (e.g. from $navigating.to) in NavItem. Then tighten the nav check in interaction-perf.e2e.ts to maxFrame 2.

title: Encode the blurred photo backdrop smaller (~1.7s CPU per 2560x1440 AVIF)
description: Found in PR #73: on-demand thumbnails can wait ~2-4s on one core behind the one background prerender, because the blurred backdrop is encoded at full 2560x1440 AVIF (~1.7s CPU each). A blurred image can be encoded much smaller and scaled up by the browser with no visible loss. Also consider (human, protected config) trace: 'retain-on-failure' in playwright.config.ts so flaky CI e2e failures are diagnosable.

title: Portrait header: clock wraps to 4 lines beside Sleep/Lock on non-home screens

Adding whitespace-nowrap in Clock.svelte caused horizontal overflow (child-switcher e2e), so it needs a header layout tweak. Overlaps hub-5fd.6 (AppShell header); do after it merges.

title: Adult logout cannot revoke copied session cookies
description: Sessions are signed cookies with no server state, so /api/auth/logout only clears the cookie; a copied cookie stays valid until expiry. Consider a session version counter in settings bumped on logout (found in PR #55).

title: Exclude src/service-worker in tsconfig.json (SvelteKit tsconfig_invalid warning)
description: PR #48 adds src/service-worker.ts; SvelteKit warns 'src/service-worker should be added to exclude'. tsconfig.json is protected -> needs human-approved.
notes: Lead investigated 2026-10-16: adding "exclude": ["src/service-worker"] alone would silence the warning but stop type-checking src/service-worker.ts (svelte-check only uses ./tsconfig.json). SvelteKit 3's intended setup is src/service-worker/index.ts plus src/service-worker/tsconfig.json extending $app/tsconfig/service-worker (lib ESNext+WebWorker), the main tsconfig excluding it, and a second type check (e.g. tsc --noEmit -p src/service-worker) in the package.json check script, which is protected. Low value (only a warning) for several protected changes. Deferred; needs a human decision on whether it's worth it.

title: Amend ADR 0001: plain fetch instead of googleapis for Google Calendar
